title: California Man Identified as Cole Tomas Allen in Custody After Shooting at Dinner Attended by Trump
partialText: Shots were fired at the hotel hosting the White House correspondents’ dinner. Authorities said the attack was carried out by a lone gunman who was brought down by the Secret Service.

title: Trump Describes His Mind-Set After Shooting at White House Correspondents’ Dinner
partialText: Very little was clear about what had happened at the Washington Hilton on Saturday night. But the president wanted to talk about it.

title: Iran and U.S. Sink Into Awkward Limbo of ‘No War, No Peace’
partialText: Each side is betting it can last longer than the other, analysts say. But there are risks in a stalemate without a deal.

title: How the War in Iran Is Draining the U.S. of Critical Weapons
partialText: The United States has blown through weapons as the cost of the war in Iran has hit nearly $1 billion a day. Our national security correspondent Eric Schmitt explains how American costs may go beyond the financial.

title: U.S. Sanctions Zigzag in New World of Economic Warfare
partialText: With oil prices in mind, the Trump administration has deployed a haphazard approach to sanctions on Russia and Iran.

title: Israel and Hezbollah Trade Strikes in Lebanon, as Iran Talks Remain on Hold
partialText: Cease-fires in Lebanon and Iran are on shaky ground, with military attacks flaring and direct talks between Washington and Tehran to end their war stalled.

title: Thom Tillis Is Prepared to Advance Kevin Warsh After U.S. Drops Fed Inquiry
partialText: Senator Thom Tillis said he had received assurances from federal prosecutors that eased his concerns, setting the stage for a key committee vote on Kevin Warsh.

title: The Trump Administration Has Changed Almost Every Aspect of Food Stamps
partialText: Legislation and regulatory tweaks enacted over the past year have altered who is eligible, what recipients can buy and how much some receive in benefits, among other changes.

title: The Hard Life of an Immigrant Whose Killing Became a Symbol for Trump
partialText: President Trump posted surveillance footage of Nilufa Easmin’s brutal killing by another immigrant to advance his agenda. Behind the rhetoric was a more nuanced story.

title: Israel’s President, Putting Off Decision on Pardon for Netanyahu, Will Push for Plea Deal
partialText: President Isaac Herzog of Israel has decided not to issue a pardon to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his corruption case at this time, and instead will seek mediation, officials say.

title: 40 Years After the Meltdown, War Layers Another Disaster on Chernobyl
partialText: Ideas have been floated for how the contaminated zone could bring economic benefits to Ukraine. But for the foreseeable future, it will be an army-controlled security belt.

title: 40 Years Ago, a Nuclear Catastrophe at Chernobyl
partialText: Photographs from the first days of the Chernobyl disaster and of the aftermath years later show the response, the evacuation and the long-term consequences of the world’s worst nuclear accident.

title: Dwarkesh Patel’s Podcast Lets You Eavesdrop on the A.I. Elite
partialText: Dwarkesh Patel was a bored college sophomore looking for intellectual stimulation. Now he commands interviews with Jensen Huang and Mark Zuckerberg and holds his own with deeply nerdy A.I. researchers.

title: ‘It Wasn’t Real, but It Was Real’
partialText: How ICE transformed a Chicago neighborhood.

title: MAHA Propelled Kennedy to the White House. It May Become His Downfall.
partialText: MAHA propelled Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to the White House. It may become his downfall.

title: A Shooting in Washington
partialText: We have the latest on the shooting at the White House correspondents’ dinner.

title: South Carolina Measles Outbreak Ends After Sickening Nearly 1,000
partialText: It was the largest outbreak in recent U.S. history.

title: Supreme Court to Hear Arguments in Landmark Roundup Weedkiller Case
partialText: A victory for the manufacturer, Bayer, could end thousands of lawsuits against the company claiming that the herbicide causes cancer.
